# Parenting questions we saved

Answers copied from a parenting website's FAQ pages, printed for the fridge binder.

## My baby has a fever, when should I worry?

Fever is the body's normal response to an infection and is usually not dangerous by itself. Keep your baby comfortable, offer fluids and watch how they act. Call your pediatrician if you are worried, if the fever goes on, or if your baby seems very sick.

## Should I take my child to the emergency room?

Go to the emergency room if your child is struggling to breathe, has a seizure, cannot be woken, or looks very ill. For anything else, call your pediatrician's office or the after-hours nurse line first and describe what you are seeing.

## Is it okay to give my child fever medicine?

Fever medicine can make a child more comfortable, but it does not treat the cause. Follow the dose on the label for your child's weight and age, and ask your pediatrician if you are not sure which one to use.

## My child bumped their head, should I be worried?

Most bumps on the head are minor. Comfort your child, hold a cold pack on any swelling, and keep an eye on how they behave over the next day. Call your doctor if you are worried about anything you see.

## What should I do about a bee sting or a bug bite?

Wash the area with soap and water and use a cold pack to ease the pain and swelling. Watch for any sign of an allergic reaction, and call your doctor if you are concerned.

## How do I treat a burn at home?

Cool the burn, keep it clean and covered, and do not break any blisters. A burn that is large, deep or on the face needs a doctor.

## Can my child take cold medicine and allergy medicine together?

Many children's cold and allergy products overlap, so ask your pharmacist or pediatrician before you combine them. Never give a child an adult medicine.

## How do I take my child's temperature?

Use a digital thermometer. Under the tongue or in the ear works for older children, and a baby's temperature is best taken with a rectal thermometer. Wait 30 minutes after a bath or a hot drink and take it again if the first reading seems off.

## When can my child go back to school?

When the fever has been gone for a full day without medicine, they are eating and drinking normally, and they feel well enough to sit through class.

## My child has a burn with blisters, what should I do?

A burn that blisters is a second-degree burn. Keep the area clean and covered, and do not pop the blisters. Call your doctor if the burn is large, or on the face, hands or feet.
